::: {.callout-note}
## About this page

This page **tests how the viewer opens figures of different shapes**:
very wide collages (25 × 2 inches), tall strips, a poster, a portrait
photo and a small plot, alone, in galleries and in layouts, and the `fit`
option. All are png; other formats are on [E: image formats](e-formats.html).

By default (`fit: auto`) very wide figures open at screen height from the
left end (or where they were clicked), very tall ones at screen width from
the top, and everything else whole, never enlarged past its real size.

Headings carry what the browser test checks: `expect-fit` (`contain`,
`height` or `width`), `shift-scroll` (which way Shift+scroll moves the
image: `x` sideways, `y` up and down, `none`, or `zoomed-x`: sideways
after zooming in until the image extends past the screen both ways) and
`expect-scale="1"` (opens at real size). The first single collage and
image shown whole also get the focal point and containment checks.
:::

```{r}
#| include: false

# A collage: `n` panels side by side, like a wide patchwork figure.
collage <- function(n = 12) {
  set.seed(1)
  par(mfrow = c(1, n), mar = c(3, 3, 2, 1))
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    plot(cumsum(rnorm(200)), type = "l", main = paste("Panel", i),
         xlab = "", ylab = "", col = hcl.colors(n)[i], lwd = 2)
  }
}

# A tall strip: `n` rows stacked, like a tall patchwork figure.
strip <- function(seed = 2, n = 8) {
  set.seed(seed)
  par(mfrow = c(n, 1), mar = c(2, 3, 2, 1))
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    plot(cumsum(rnorm(100)), type = "l", main = paste("Row", i), xlab = "", ylab = "")
  }
}

wave <- function(k = 1) {
  x <- seq(0, 4 * pi, length.out = 400)
  plot(x, sin(k * x), type = "l", lwd = 2, col = hcl.colors(4)[k],
       main = paste("Wave", k), xlab = "x", ylab = "sin(kx)")
}
```

## 1. Wide collage, png (25 × 2 in) {#c1 expect-fit="height" shift-scroll="x"}

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 25
#| fig-height: 2
#| fig-cap: "A 25 × 2 inch collage of 12 panels (png)."

collage()
```

## 2. Wide collage with `fit: contain` {#c2 expect-fit="contain" shift-scroll="none"}

The override for case 1: the whole collage, as a strip.

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   fit: contain
#| fig-width: 25
#| fig-height: 2
#| fig-cap: "The collage, forced to open whole."

collage()
```

## 3. Moderately wide figure (16 × 4 in) {#c3 expect-fit="contain"}

Wide, but readable whole: the size rule leaves it alone.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "A 4:1 figure."

collage(4)
```

## 4. Tall strip (4 × 15 in) {#c4 expect-fit="width" shift-scroll="y"}

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 15
#| fig-cap: "A tall strip of 8 panels."

set.seed(2)
par(mfrow = c(8, 1), mar = c(2, 3, 2, 1))
for (i in 1:8) plot(cumsum(rnorm(100)), type = "l", main = paste("Row", i), xlab = "", ylab = "")
```

## 5. Large poster (24 × 18 in) {#c5 expect-fit="contain" shift-scroll="zoomed-x"}

Opens whole; zoomed in, it extends past the screen both ways, and
Shift+scroll moves sideways.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 24
#| fig-height: 18
#| fig-cap: "A 24 × 18 inch poster of 48 panels."

set.seed(3)
par(mfrow = c(6, 8), mar = c(2, 2, 2, 1))
for (i in 1:48) plot(cumsum(rnorm(100)), type = "l", main = paste("Panel", i), xlab = "", ylab = "")
```

## 6. Portrait photo {#c6 expect-fit="contain"}

An ordinary 9:16 photo is not a strip: it opens whole, on any screen width
(the test also checks this in a 2560 px wide window).

![A portrait photo.](../../images/mv-4.jpg){.panzoom width=30%}

## 7. Small plot (288 × 192 px) {#c7 expect-fit="contain" expect-scale="1"}

Opens at its real size, centered, rather than enlarged to fill the
screen; scroll still zooms in (up to `max-zoom`).

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 3
#| fig-height: 2
#| fig-dpi: 48
#| fig-cap: "A small plot."

plot(pressure)
```

## 8. `fit: height` on an ordinary plot {#c8 expect-open="panzoom" expect-fit="height"}

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   fit: height

wave(3)
```

## 9. `fit: width` on an ordinary plot {#c9 expect-open="panzoom" expect-fit="width"}

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   fit: width

wave(4)
```

## 10. Gallery of two collages {#c10 expect-fit="height"}

Left/Right and drags pan along the collage; PageDown, PageUp and the
buttons switch collages.

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   group: collages
#| fig-width: 25
#| fig-height: 2
#| fig-cap:
#|   - "First collage."
#|   - "Second collage."

collage()
collage(15)
```

## 11. Gallery of two tall strips {#c11 expect-fit="width"}

Each strip opens at screen width and extends downwards: Left/Right do
nothing (there is nowhere to go sideways) rather than switch strips;
PageDown, PageUp and the buttons switch.

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   group: strips
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 15
#| fig-cap:
#|   - "First strip."
#|   - "Second strip."

for (k in 1:2) {
  set.seed(10 + k)
  par(mfrow = c(8, 1), mar = c(2, 3, 2, 1))
  for (i in 1:8) plot(cumsum(rnorm(100)), type = "l", main = paste("Strip", k, "row", i), xlab = "", ylab = "")
}
```

## 12. Two collages stacked (layout-nrow: 2) {#c12 expect-fit="height"}

Subfigures in a layout: each opens on its own at screen height, and the
two form a gallery.

```{r}
#| label: fig-collage-rows
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 25
#| fig-height: 2
#| fig-cap: "Two collages, stacked."
#| fig-subcap: ["First collage", "Second collage"]
#| layout-nrow: 2

collage()
collage(15)
```

## 13. Two tall strips side by side (layout-ncol: 2) {#c13 expect-fit="width"}

```{r}
#| label: fig-strip-cols
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 15
#| fig-cap: "Two tall strips, side by side."
#| fig-subcap: ["First strip", "Second strip"]
#| layout-ncol: 2

strip(2)
strip(3)
```

## 14. Tall strips in a layout div {#c14 expect-fit="width"}

A `.panzoom` div with a layout, around two separate code cells: each
strip opens on its own (no gallery: they are not subfigures).

::: {.panzoom layout-ncol="2"}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 15

strip(4)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 15

strip(5)
```

:::
